resources.string: Share redacted recent events and the last crash record.

Share recent events and the last crash record, if available, including the app version, Android API level and device model. Addresses, user-assigned device and host names, PINs, credentials and exception messages are omitted. Add what happened when sharing. Nothing is sent until you choose an app.
Could not share the report. Check free storage and install an app that can share text files, then try again.
You can share a report with technical crash details to help diagnose the problem. Nothing is sent automatically.
The previous stream was interrupted. Open your PC and resume the game to reconnect.
Apply Balanced, Low latency, Best quality or Battery saver settings.

Sets bitrate, frame rate, variable refresh and frame pacing together. Low latency keeps your codec; Auto prefers low-latency AV1, then HEVC, then H.264. Except Battery saver, presets use the screen’s maximum refresh rate (up to 1000 FPS). Per-PC video profiles override global video values; VRR always requests the screen’s maximum rate. Resolution and HDR stay as you set them.
Preset applied. Per-PC video profiles still take priority.

resources.string: Fill the screen; the image may look wider or taller.
Choose how frames balance response time and smooth motion; VRR overrides this.
Choose the language used by the app.
Compact shows shown FPS, total latency (network + decode) and frame loss. Advanced shows all measurements. Long-press the overlay to switch.
Turn on the performance overlay and wait for a video frame to copy stats.

Measures 10 host requests for latency, jitter and failed requests. On supported paired hosts, also downloads 32 MiB to measure bandwidth. This can use mobile data and briefly slow other traffic. Settings stay unchanged.
Testing the connection… Leave this screen or tap Cancel to stop.

Latency is the average host-request round trip. Jitter is the average change between consecutive successful requests. Probe loss counts failed HTTP requests, not lost UDP packets. During a stream, the performance overlay shows transport delay and lost video frames.
Bandwidth: unavailable. Pair with a host that supports the bandwidth test to measure throughput.
Bandwidth test could not finish. Check that the PC is awake, the host is running and both devices can reach each other, then try again.
For lower delay or fewer failures, use the same Wi-Fi network, move closer to the router, connect the PC by Ethernet and pause other downloads.
Could not reach the pairing service. Keep the PC awake, open the host app and connect both devices to the same network. Allow the host through the PC firewall, then try again.
Learn how to wake a sleeping PC from the app.

1. Connect and pair while the PC is awake so its network address can be saved.

2. Enable Wake-on-LAN in the PC firmware and network adapter settings (often called Wake on Magic Packet).

3. Keep the PC connected by Ethernet and try waking it from sleep on the same home network. Wi-Fi, shutdown and waking across routers depend on the PC and network.

4. Long-press an offline PC and choose Wake PC. If it stays asleep, check adapter power settings; the app cannot confirm delivery of a wake packet.
